thread:
Indra: Quick question — we want to shorten the ephemeral request-cache TTL for 'router-service' from 30d -> 7d to cut storage costs. Any compliance or redaction blockers? Do we need a scrub job or is expiry enough? Who needs to sign off?

Claire: Which cache specifically? response-cache or request-cache? small change can break debugging if we lose traces.

Indra: request-cache (holds raw prompts + small response fragments). Used for quick retries, not full traces.

Pete-Sec: Heads up — if raw prompts are stored, that is customer data. Shortening TTL is fine from a privacy perspective but we must ensure any persisted copies that land in logs/metrics are redacted. Please confirm where the objects live (S3/RocksDB) and whether we log request bodies somewhere else. Also we need Security + Legal acknowledgment if this will remove stored customer content earlier than the contracted retention windows. Policy reference: https://redwood.example.com/policies/data-retention

ops-bot: Ticket created: INF-4321 "router-service request-cache TTL change". Assigned to @Claire.

Lia: If it's only local RocksDB/ephemeral cache and not part of the audit logs, 7d seems reasonable. If any ingestion pipeline snapshots include the cache contents, we need to scrub them or mark the snapshot as transient and update retention. Suggest: (a) document exact storage, (b) add a lightweight redaction step to the eviction path that zeroes prompt bodies, or (c) hash prefixes before writing to disk.

Indra: It does persist to a per-region RocksDB and we also occasionally run an async dump to S3 for hot rewarm. The dump is the scary part.

Pete-Sec: Ok — for S3 dumps we must run a one-off scrub for past objects that contain prompts. Recommended path: 1) run a discovery job to enumerate keys older than 7d and sample contents; 2) if prompts present, run an MFA-protected scrub job to delete or redact; 3) add a pre-dump transformation to strip prompt bodies (or hash them) going forward; 4) notify Legal if removal would shorten retention below customer contract terms. I can sign off after we see the discovery samples and the proposed redaction script.

Claire: I'll take INF-4321 and do the discovery. Plan to run a canary sample on staging Friday. @Pete-Sec can you review the sample output once uploaded? I'll paste queries and a minimal scrub script.

Pete-Sec: Yep, will review. For the scrub script include a dry-run mode and an idempotent delete path. Also include audit logs for which keys were removed (only metadata, not full bodies).

Indra: Thanks all — I'll stop the S3 dump job until Claire's canary finishes.

Lia: One operational note — ensure your runbook includes a rollback: short TTL -> increased error rates when cold rewarm hits. Consider a brief traffic-steady window after rollout.

Claire: Noted. Will include smoke checks and a 24h rollback window in the RFC.

Pete-Sec: Final checklist from Sec side: discovery samples uploaded to secure bucket, scrub script with dry-run, runbook w/ rollback and audit entries, Legal ack if contract windows affected. After those 4 items I'm happy to sign off.

Indra: Got it — we'll proceed that way. Thanks! :+1:
